question.text: `Hariyali Foundation`, a forest-conservation NPO in Odisha, receives a EUR 2 lakh grant from a German CSR donor. Under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act 2010 (FCRA), the first receipt of this foreign contribution must land in:

answer.text: Any scheduled commercial bank branch designated by the NPO's Board
The Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai
Any FCRA-registered sub-account at an Authorised Dealer Category-I branch
The State Bank of India, New Delhi Main Branch (FCRA Account)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act 2010 as amended in 2020, every NPO that receives foreign contribution must do so first into a designated 'FCRA Account' opened at the State Bank of India, New Delhi Main Branch. Subsequent utilisation can move to FCRA utilisation accounts at other scheduled banks, but the first receipt of foreign contribution must land in the SBI NDMB FCRA Account. The Trap: Receipt at any scheduled commercial bank reflects the pre-2020 position and is no longer permissible. The RBI is not the receiver of foreign contribution under FCRA. Authorised Dealer Cat-I accounts belong to the FEMA framework, not FCRA receipt. Note: The cited SIA workbook supports that FCRA governs foreign donations and contributions to NPOs, but it does not on the pages checked specifically state that first receipt must land in the SBI New Delhi Main Branch FCRA Account. The framing above reflects the current FCRA legislative framework rather than a workbook-page citation.
